card.name: Verbs just before an effect on something
card.fires_on: The helping verb or subject-ending word right after a cause, where the next words describe its effect on something ("are having an impact on", "can alter", "increased"). Fires in cause-and-effect statements.

modes.label: Impact phrasing
modes.description: A form of 'be' or 'to' right before 'having/have an impact on' something.
modes.example: their lifestyle<< is>> having on the environment

modes.label: Drug interaction effect
modes.description: The closing parenthesis or drug name right before 'increased' in interaction findings.
modes.example: Daily oral dosing of paroxetine (30 mg once daily<<)>> increased steady-state AUC 0-

modes.label: Cause can change outcome
modes.description: A modal verb after a cause noun, before a verb like lower or alter.
modes.example: during pregnancy<< can>> alter the DNA of her child

card.writes: It pushes the model toward 'having' and away from 'impact', as the next word after the verb.
card.plain: It fires where a cause is about to be said to affect something else.
